# Diagnostics, Audit, and Run Inspection

Yantra keeps diagnostics and run evidence on the local machine so you can check whether the environment is ready, find earlier runs, inspect what happened, and retrieve the resulting report without contacting a remote telemetry service.

## What It Does

### Environment diagnostics

`yantra doctor` runs offline checks and reports an overall `ok`, `warn`, or `fail` status. It does not open a model-provider session. The current checks cover:

- `browser.selection` — which browser a run would actually use: the configured source and whether it
  came from `config.yaml` or the default, plus ownership, canonical executable, and actual version. A
  selection that resolves to nothing reports the typed error with its remediation and the alternatives
  discovery found.
- `browser.compatibility` — the last local compatibility evidence recorded for that browser, reported
  as passed, failed, `unverified` when nothing has been checked yet, or `stale` when the evidence
  describes a different binary. Doctor never launches a browser to produce a verdict, and a build
  newer than the driver's tested pairing reads as `capability-checked` normal operation rather than a
  warning.
- `browser.managed` — the Yantra-managed browser root, the ready build or `absent`, and the orphan
  count with reclaimable bytes. Doctor reports those totals; it never installs or reclaims anything.

  Both `--json` and the terminal also carry one browser provenance block with the same source, origin,
  ownership, executable, version, compatibility, managed root, orphan totals, alternatives, and
  remediation. See [Browser Selection and Diagnostics](browser-selection-and-diagnostics.md) and
  [Browser Resolution and Lifecycle](browser-resolution-and-lifecycle.md).

- Write access to the Yantra data and cache directories.
- Data-directory permissions. On Windows this check is best-effort; on POSIX systems it warns when the data or profile directories are accessible to group or other users.
- An OS-keychain write/read/delete round trip.
- Opening, migrating, and writing the local SQLite history index. If the index is corrupt, doctor moves it aside, rebuilds it from run directories, and reports a warning.
- The effective agent provider, model, and thinking selection, including whether each value came from a flag, environment variable, profile preference, or pinned default.
- Whether an agent credential source is available. Missing credentials are a warning because deterministic use is still valid.
- `search.provider` — which web-search provider an agentic run would use, chosen by the same selection rules a run applies, without building the provider or starting a browser. It is `ok` for a keyed API provider and a warning for a scraped one, because a run asks a scraped provider one query at a time and stops searching after its first challenge; the fix hint is ``Run `yantra secret set tavily.api_key` or `yantra secret set brave.api_key` to use a keyed provider.`` A selection that cannot resolve, such as an explicitly configured keyed provider with no key, is an error carrying that failure's message. `--json` also carries a top-level `search: {provider, kind, via}` block.
- The wall-clock, provider-token, tool-timeout, retry, and confirmation-wait budgets that agentic commands will use, their configuration sources, and whether each stored value is parseable. This check **fails** when it is not, so a malformed `YANTRA_AGENT_MAX_DURATION` surfaces here rather than at the start of your next agentic run. `profile.yaml` values are schema-validated when written, so a failure normally names an environment variable, and the remediation names the offending source directly.

Doctor reports the health of stored state, so per-run budget flags are not part of its surface: it registers `--provider`, `--model`, `--thinking`, `--auth-secret`, and `--no-llm`, and rejects `--max-duration`, `--max-tokens`, `--tool-timeout`, `--tool-retries`, `--confirm-timeout`, and `--no-screenshots`. Model-selection flags belong because they choose which credential is probed and which model `--agent-smoke` targets.

Under `--no-llm` or `LLM_PROVIDER=none` the three `agent.*` checks report that the deterministic path was selected and name the layer that selected it, no credential is probed, and budgets are not validated — none of them would be used.

Core environment-probe results are cached for one hour; agent model, credential, and budget diagnostics and the configuration checks are recalculated on each invocation. `--refresh` bypasses the core cache only. The cache is additionally keyed on the effective browser identity — the configured selection, the canonical executable with its version and size/timestamp, the managed ready pointer, and the orphan count — so changing your browser selection produces fresh output without `--refresh`. Warnings do not fail the command; any failed check exits `3`.

`yantra doctor --agent-smoke` is different: it is a live, billable provider check. It opens one fresh provider session in Yantra's pinned environment, exposes only a `status` tool, asks the model to call it once, streams normalized events, prints the effective pinned paths and zero ambient-resource counts, and closes the session. The raw provider session is saved below a timestamped `runs/agent-smoke-.../agent/` directory.

The smoke passes only if the provider run completes and the `status` tool succeeds. It has no deterministic fallback: missing credentials, an unknown model, an unreachable provider, or a failed round trip exits `3`; Ctrl+C tears down the session and exits `130`. With `--json` the smoke suppresses the event stream and the human summary and emits one `doctor_smoke` envelope instead. Its directory is not a normal auditable run because it has no `manifest.json`.

### Run discovery and inspection

`yantra list` defaults to recent runs. It merges the rebuildable SQLite history index with readable filesystem run manifests, de-duplicates by run ID, sorts newest first, and can filter by workflow name or status. If the index is unavailable, it warns on stderr and continues with the filesystem scan. `yantra list workflows` lists saved workflows instead.

`yantra show <target>` displays either a saved workflow definition or a run manifest plus recent events. An ISO-prefixed target is treated as a run ID; other targets are treated as workflow names. `--run` and `--workflow` override that detection. Run inspection is read-only, skips malformed event lines, and shows the most recent 20 events by default.

`yantra usage` reads the local history index and groups task count and recorded cost by UTC day and provider. It can filter by task type and start time. If the index is unavailable, it returns an empty result with a rebuild hint and exits successfully; it does not scan run files itself.

### Audit and report views

`yantra audit <run-id>` builds a read-only trust narrative from Yantra-owned projections in the run directory. It reports run status and timing, workflow or command name, step and security-scope counts, secret lookup keys, agent provider/model/prompt provenance, tool calls in sequence order, confirmation linkage, provider usage, and a typed terminal startup error when present. A scheduled run's `schedule.json` adds schedule-fire narration, including the pause-and-notify guarantee for pending confirmations.

Audit never reads the raw provider session to construct structured output. A tool call with a `start` entry but no matching `end` entry is shown as incomplete rather than assigned a guessed result. Missing optional files and malformed JSONL lines are skipped; a missing or unreadable `manifest.json` is fatal. The audit command does not take a run lock or change the run directory.

Browser fill and click entries may carry `details.attempted`: the recovery ledger projected to verdicts. The same projection goes into the tool result the model sees and into the sanitized `tool-calls.jsonl` record, so audit reads what the model read. Every record carries `ordinal`, `strategy`, `axis`, and a `verdict` of `succeeded`, `failed`, or `skipped`. A skipped record carries `unmet` and nothing else, because it spent no work; a failed record carries `error_code` and an optional `detail`. `error_code` appears on failed records only — elsewhere it is absent, never `null`. The measured fields `entry_evidence`, `charged_actions`, `remaining_actions`, and `elapsed_ms` are omitted unless they say something: a key is never written as an empty list or as zero, so a field's presence means that record actually measured it.

Succeeded and failed records may also carry a fixed allowlist of scalar rung evidence — `substituted`, `substitution_position`, `tie_break`, `scroll_steps`, `scroll_stop`, `revealed_driver`, and `reacquisitions`. Nothing else a recovery rung produced is serialized, so no page text and no container path can reach the ledger through evidence. The serialized ledger is bounded at 24 records; when a run produces more, the first record and the last 23 are kept, and the gap is visible from the retained ordinals rather than silent.

Reading is backward compatible and read-only. Audit and report readers accept the legacy nullable attempt-record shape and the verdict shape alike, normalize either in memory, and stay total over arbitrary JSON — a malformed record reads as a described placeholder (`error_code: "MALFORMED_ATTEMPT_RECORD"`, or `unmet: "malformed-artifact"` when it was skipped) instead of failing the read. Measured fields stay optional on the way in: a legacy record that never measured `charged_actions` reads as absent rather than as zero. The one remaining producer of the legacy shape is the controller's `clear-obstruction` record on the click path, which is converted at the tool boundary and appears in `attempted` as an ordinary verdict alongside the plan's own. Readers never rewrite the source `tool-calls.jsonl` or any run directory.

`yantra report <run-id>` prints the run's existing `report.md` verbatim. `--open` launches `$EDITOR`, or `notepad.exe`, `open`, or `xdg-open` when `$EDITOR` is unset. `--open` cannot be combined with `--json`. Audit and report serve different purposes: audit reconstructs structured evidence from stable projections, while report returns the already-rendered Markdown outcome.

An agentic `report.md` lists `- runtime.jsonl` under its `## Audit Trail` heading, and only when that file exists in the run directory. The report checks presence alone: neither it nor `yantra audit` parses the runtime log or derives run status from it, so a run directory that has none renders exactly as it otherwise would. See [Run artifacts](#run-artifacts) for what the log holds.

An agentic `report.md` also renders a `## Run Health` section, placed directly after `## Tool Calls`, when the run directory holds a `run-health.json` that validates against the protocol `RunHealth` schema:

```text
## Run Health
Searches: 3 total, 1 ok, 2 failed (SEARCH_BLOCKED 2) - providers: duckduckgo
Fetches: 4 total (3 http, 1 browser), 1 repeat - failed: FETCH_TIMEOUT 1
Source failures: fetch 1, extract 0, blocked 0, budget 2, policy 0
Browser launches: 1
Navigations: 12/12   Hosts: 5/8   Exhausted: navigations
Tool failures: 3 (SEARCH_BLOCKED 2, FETCH_TIMEOUT 1)
Notices: 3
Extraction: pages collection 2, detail 3 - records shown 30 - links offered 64, withheld 1, followed 4
```

The `Extraction:` line appears only when the file has an `extraction` block. It lists the page reads returned to the agent by shape, then records shown, links offered and withheld, and links followed (`discovered_follows`), and holds no URL or page text. The section renders only these lines; the acquisition counters described under [`run-health.json`](#run-healthjson), such as store hits, challenge pages, and page-pool launches, are in the file and the `run_health` line but not in `report.md`. Code lists are ordered by descending count, then by code. The parenthesized failure codes, the `- failed:` fetch list, and the tool-failure codes appear only when there is something to list, and `providers` and `Exhausted` read `none` when empty. A `run-health.json` that exists but cannot be read or does not validate renders the single line `Run Health: run-health.json unreadable` in place of the section. A run directory without the file renders no section at all, so reports of older runs are unchanged. `- run-health.json` is listed under `## Audit Trail` whenever the file is present, readable or not. `yantra audit` does not read `run-health.json`.

When the run declared a task contract, `report.md` renders a `## Task Contract` section directly after `## Tool Calls` and before `## Run Health`. It lists the current (last) revision and the revision count:

```text
## Task Contract
Deliverable: table - new SUV listings
Required fields: seller, price, exterior color, interior color
Filters: drivetrain=AWD
Required sources: example.com
Revisions: 1
```

`Required fields`, `Filters`, and `Required sources` read `none` when empty; `Ranking: <field> <asc|desc>`, `Limit: <n>`, and `Notes: <text>` appear only when set. A `contract.json` that cannot be read or does not validate against the protocol `TaskContractRecord` schema renders the single line `Task Contract: contract.json present but invalid` and never fails the report. A run without the file renders no section. `- contract.json` is listed under `## Audit Trail` whenever the file is present, readable or not.

## How to Use It

Check the local environment, then bypass the one-hour cache after changing Chrome, permissions, credentials, or model settings:

```bash
yantra doctor
yantra doctor --json
yantra doctor --refresh
```

Run the live provider smoke with the same model-selection flags used by agentic commands:

```bash
yantra doctor --agent-smoke --provider ollama --model llama3.1:8b
yantra doctor --agent-smoke --provider anthropic --model claude-haiku-4-5
yantra doctor --agent-smoke --json
```

The smoke also accepts `--thinking` and `--auth-secret`. Deterministic selection through `--no-llm` or `LLM_PROVIDER=none` is incompatible with live smoke and exits `1`, naming whichever of the two selected it; unavailable credentials exit `3`.

Find and inspect runs:

```bash
yantra list
yantra list runs --limit 5
yantra list runs --workflow quarterly-report --status failed
yantra list workflows

yantra show <run-id>
yantra show <run-id> --events 100
yantra show <run-id> --run --json
yantra show quarterly-report --workflow
```

Render the trust narrative or retrieve the report:

```bash
yantra audit <run-id>
yantra audit <run-id> --json
yantra report <run-id>
yantra report <run-id> --json
yantra report <run-id> --open
```

Review local task volume and recorded cost:

```bash
yantra usage
yantra usage --type ask --since 7d
yantra usage --type research --since 24h
yantra usage --since 2026-08-01 --json
```

Valid usage types are `ask`, `research`, `run`, and `do`. `--since` accepts `YYYY-MM-DD`, a whole number of days such as `7d`, or a whole number of hours such as `24h`.

## Inputs and Outputs

### Run IDs and local paths

Normal runs live under `<yantra-data-dir>/runs/<run-id>/`. Everything Yantra owns lives under one root, `~/.yantra` (override `YANTRA_HOME`), identically on Windows, macOS, and Linux, so the default data directory is `~/.yantra/data`. Run IDs are lexicographically sortable and normally include a compact UTC timestamp, command or workflow name, and short random suffix.

The doctor cache lives at `~/.yantra/cache/doctor.json` on every platform, or below `paths.cache_dir` / `YANTRA_CACHE_DIR` when the cache directory has been relocated.

### JSON envelopes

`doctor`, `list`, `show`, `audit`, and `report` wrap JSON output in a single object containing the current protocol `schemaVersion` and a command-specific `kind`. Representative shapes are:

```json
{
  "schemaVersion": "<current>",
  "kind": "doctor",
  "checks": [],
  "overall": "ok",
  "version": "<protocol>",
  "platform": "win32",
  "nodeVersion": "<node>"
}
```

`doctor --agent-smoke --json` emits its own kind, because the live smoke reports
one session rather than a list of environment checks:

```json
{
  "schemaVersion": "<current>",
  "kind": "doctor_smoke",
  "outcome": "passed",
  "provider": "anthropic",
  "model": "claude-haiku-4-5",
  "runId": "agent-smoke-<timestamp>",
  "runDir": "<yantra-data-dir>/runs/agent-smoke-<timestamp>",
  "sessionId": "<provider session>",
  "logPath": "<runDir>/agent/<session>.jsonl",
  "stopReason": "stop",
  "statusToolInvoked": true,
  "usage": { "turns": 1 },
  "environment": {
    "agentDir": "<pinned>",
    "authPath": "<pinned>",
    "modelsPath": "<pinned>",
    "settingsSource": "in-memory",
    "extensions": 0,
    "skills": 0,
    "prompts": 0,
    "themes": 0,
    "contextFiles": 0
  }
}
```

`outcome` is `passed`, `failed`, or `aborted`, matching exit codes `0`, `3`, and `130`.

```json
{
  "schemaVersion": "<current>",
  "kind": "audit",
  "runId": "<run-id>",
  "status": "completed",
  "toolCalls": [],
  "usage": null
}
```

```json
{ "schemaVersion": "<current>", "kind": "report", "markdown": "# Run report\n..." }
```

`list --json` returns `kind: "list"` with an `items` array; `show --json` returns `kind: "show"` with one `item`. `usage --json` returns `schemaVersion`, `kind: "usage"`, `rows`, and aggregate `totals`; an unavailable index also adds a `note`. These inspection commands emit one final JSON object, not the progress NDJSON used by live agentic commands.

### Run artifacts

Files vary by command and by how far a run progressed. The common and diagnostic artifacts are:

| Artifact                               | User-visible purpose                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| -------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `manifest.json`                        | Canonical run identity, status, timestamps, redacted parameters, output bindings, and optional agent/synthesis metadata. Agent metadata records provider/model, credential source, session pointer, prompt version/hash, and tool-catalog hash, never credential material.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| `events.jsonl`                         | Append-only task lifecycle: start, step, retry, checkpoint, confirmation, handoff, completion, failure, and related events.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| `plan.json` and `checkpoints/`         | Validated replay plan and saved continuation points for workflow runs.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| `outputs.json`                         | Declared workflow outputs, subject to the workflow's retention and redaction rules.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| `report.md`                            | Human-readable completion, failure, handoff, and resume guidance.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| `agent/<session>.jsonl`                | Raw provider conversation/session log for agentic runs. `manifest.agent.session_file` is a relative pointer to it.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| `tool-calls.jsonl`                     | Stable, schema-validated start/end projection of agent tools with sanitized inputs/outputs, status, duration, error code, optional confirmation ID, and browser-recovery verdicts where applicable.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| `runtime.jsonl`                        | Operator-only local diagnostics for agentic runs: which browser and driver ran, why that pairing was accepted, where its compatibility evidence came from, the safe class of a startup or unexpected tool failure, one closed-field line per failed tool call, the selected search provider, search-breaker, fetch-escalation, and challenge-page events by hostname, and the run's health summary. Never model input and never a published result.                                                                                                                                                                 |
| `run-health.json`                      | An agentic run's own account of what happened to it: searches by outcome and failure code, network fetches by mode, reads answered without a fetch, challenge pages, per-site read failures by stage, browser launches, budget use, tool failures by code, the runtime notice count, and page reads by shape with the records and links they showed. Counts, closed codes, budget names, and provider names only.                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| `contract.json`                        | The task contract an agentic `research` or `do` run declared with `task_contract`, present only when one was declared. It validates against the protocol `TaskContractRecord` schema: `schema_version: 1`, `run_id`, `command` (`research` or `do`), and `revisions`, 1 to 3 entries of `{revision, declared_at, contract}` in declaration order, the last being the current contract. It is rewritten atomically (temporary file, then rename) on every declaration, so a run that dies later still has it. Every string was sanitized before it was written. See [Task contract](agentic-tasks.md#task-contract). |
| `usage.json`                           | Per-call usage plus agent totals. In an agentic run each provider turn is one call; the `agent` block holds the reconciled session totals, where unreported token or cost values are `null`, not guessed as zero. Partial usage is retained for failed or aborted runs.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| `secrets.jsonl`                        | Secret-resolution key, step ID, and timestamp. It never stores the resolved value.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| `confirmations.jsonl`                  | Requests and human decisions used to link protected tool activity to consent.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| `captures/`                            | Oversized, sanitized web/browser extraction payloads referenced by opaque run-local IDs.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| `trace.json`                           | Successful browser interactions used for workflow promotion; secret fills retain only the secret-reference key.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| `brief.json`, `brief.md`, `brief.html` | Validated published result in portable formats when publication succeeds.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| `result.md`                            | Sanitized final assistant text salvaged when Brief publication fails; diagnostic output, not a validated Brief.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| `schedule.json`                        | Secret-free schedule/run linkage used by audit narration for daemon-fired workflows.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |

Every Brief published from agent-authored content has a non-null `metadata.citation_verdict` in `brief.json`, including a Brief assembled by the runtime from the assistant's final draft. Every model payload is sanitized and composed against the run's evidence and task contract, even if it supplies complete protocol identifiers and metadata; those fields cannot bypass the checks or supply the verdict. Its fields are `claims_checked`, `flagged`, and `stripped`; `stripped` is always `0` on this path. An editorial-only or fallback draft with no checked claims records `{claims_checked: 0, flagged: 0, stripped: 0}`. A complete protocol Brief supplied directly to the publisher API by a trusted internal caller keeps its own verdict. Current agentic manifests record prompt version `agent-v10`, whose `research` and `do` addenda teach publication with evidence IDs, cited findings, sections, tables, and constraint status.

The agent-content anchoring check uses the same deterministic numeric and content-word helpers as the synthesis citation validator. It checks cited findings, table cells (including Alternatives), cited sections, and verified constraint values against the stored page or the specific record named by an `S<n>#r<k>` reference. Numeric cells and section bodies receive numeric checks; text cells, findings, and verified constraints also require at least half their content words to appear in the cited evidence. Unicode, case, whitespace, and number grouping separators are normalized. Empty cells, `not shown on source`, and boolean cells are not checked. An unsupported value remains in the published document and adds one `uncited_claim_flagged` notice from `anchoring`, bounded to 600 characters with at most five example pointers and an overflow count. A zero verdict establishes only that the checks performed found no mismatch; it does not establish truth or detect cross-source contradictions.

A successful agent-content `result_publish` records `details.composition` in its sanitized tool-call projection. It contains counts for `cited_sources`, `consulted_sources`, `table_rows`, `alternatives_rows`, `alternatives_findings`, `constraints` (`verified`, `unverified`, `violated`), `contract_gaps`, `claims_checked`, and `flagged`. The same counts are logged as `brief_composed` after successful publication, including runtime assembly; a rejected publication emits no such line. See [Agentic Tasks](agentic-tasks.md#inputs-and-outputs) for the published structure and notices.

The four browser action tools — `browser_click`, `browser_navigate`, `browser_fill_element`, and `browser_fill_form` — also record what their page delta cost, inside the `details` payload each entry already carries. `delta_bytes` and `observation_bytes` are the UTF-8 byte lengths of the serialized delta block and of the observation shipped beside it, and `delta_omitted: "no-baseline"` stands in place of `delta_bytes` when there was no earlier model-visible frame to diff against. This is not a protocol change: the entry schema is strict and gained no field, and no new artifact or sink was added.

`summarizeDeltaCost`, exported from `@yantra/core` (`packages/core/src/audit/delta-cost.ts`), reads a run's entries and reports `calls`, `deltaBytesTotal`, `deltaBytesMax`, `observationBytesTotal`, `followUpObserveCount`, and `followUpObserveRate`, where a follow-up is a `browser_observe` whose immediately preceding call was a delta-bearing action. It is a reader only and changes no behavior. What it produces is recorded evidence, not a token-saving claim: whether the delta should one day stand in place of the full observation rather than beside it is a later decision that needs total-turn evidence, which is precisely what the follow-up rate exists to supply.

`runtime.jsonl` is the agentic run's operator log: an append-only Pino JSONL file at `<run-dir>/runtime.jsonl`, written by the agentic commands `yantra do`, `yantra ask`, and `yantra research`. Every line carries the run's `run_id`. It is local diagnostics and nothing else — it is never sent to the model, never part of a published result, never an evidence source, and never a retry signal. One run owns one log, closed after task-browser, page-pool, session, and recorder teardown and before `report.md` is built, so terminal lifecycle lines still land in it. A run that never constructs an environment, such as a location pre-flight that hands off first, legitimately has none.

Teardown runs in a fixed order: the task browser, the background page pool, the provider session, and the tool-call recorder tear down; any interaction trace is finalized; the run-health summary is computed from the now-final facts, written atomically to `run-health.json` (temporary file, then rename, validated against the schema first), and logged as the `run_health` line; the runtime log closes; and only then is `report.md` built. A failure while writing the health summary is a teardown error like the others: it never skips finalization, but it turns an otherwise published run into a failure reading `The task result was produced, but run teardown did not complete cleanly.` A run that fails during startup is finalized on its own path and writes neither `run-health.json` nor a `run_health` line.

Ten named projections carry `schema_version: 1` and stable snake_case fields; ordinary component logs keep their own fields alongside them.

| Runtime event             | What it records                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| ------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `browser_ready`           | INFO, exactly once per successful task-browser launch attempt. `selection_source`, `selection_origin`, and `selection_reason` say which browser was chosen and why; `ownership`, `browser_version`, `executable_basename`, `executable_path_sha256`, and `executable_stat_fingerprint` identify the binary; `driver_version`, `tested_build`, `probe_revision`, `probe_profile`, `compatibility_verdict`, and `pairing` (`tested` or `capability-checked`) record the pairing; `evidence_source` (`cache` or `probe`) and `evidence_checked_at` record where the compatibility evidence came from and when it was checked. A `capability-checked` pairing is the normal steady state and stays ordinary INFO, never a warning. |
| `browser_startup_failed`  | WARN, or ERROR for launch and process failures. At most once per failed startup attempt, written before rollback. Carries the startup `phase` (`resolution`, `reservation`, `compatibility`, `profile`, `identity-revalidation`, or `launch`), the `error_class`, and a closed `failure_kind` (`resolution`, `compatibility`, `install-declined`, `managed-install`, `coordination`, `launch`, `process`, or `unexpected`), plus the closed subtype fields that apply: `resolution_code`, `compatibility_failure_class`, `compatibility_profile`, `coordination_reason`, `install_code`, `install_phase`, `launch_phase`, `process_phase`, and `exit_proven`.                                                                  |
| `tool_unexpected_failure` | ERROR, written by the tool middleware when a tool throws something nothing mapped. Carries only `tool`, `operation_phase`, and `error_class`. This is what makes an unexpected site fault distinguishable from an expected browser startup refusal, even though the model receives the same generic result for the former. The same call also writes a `tool_failure` line with code `TOOL_EXECUTION_FAILED` and cause `unexpected:<ErrorClass>`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| `tool_failure`            | WARN, exactly one per tool call that ends in `error` or a timeout, written by the middleware's single outcome chokepoint. Carries `tool`, the stable `code`, and a closed `cause` token, plus `provider` when the tool used a search provider, `host` (a bare hostname, never a URL) when the tool reported one, and `budget_limit` when a run budget refused the call. A call that ends `denied` (consent refused) or `aborted` writes none.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| `fetch_challenge`         | WARN, once per challenge page the hybrid fetcher recognized at either tier, or a direct `browser_extract` snapshot recognized at the browser tier. Carries `tier` (`http` for Yantra's HTTP client, `browser` for the standard-browser render), the closed `marker` ID that matched, and the bare `host`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| `fetch_escalated`         | INFO, once per fetch the hybrid fetcher handed from the HTTP tier to one browser render. Carries the `reason` (`js-shell`, `http-error`, or `http-challenge`) and the bare `host`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| `search_breaker_open`     | WARN, at most once per run, when the search provider's first anti-bot challenge (`cause: "anomaly-challenge"`) or rate-limit refusal (`cause: "rate-limited"`) closes search for the rest of the run. Carries `provider` and `cause`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| `contract_declared`       | INFO, once per successful `task_contract` declaration. Carries `revision`, `deliverable`, `field_count`, `filter_count`, and `source_hosts` (the contract's required sources as bare hostnames). It never carries the subject, field names, filter text, or notes.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| `brief_composed`          | INFO, once after successful agent-content publication, including a runtime-assembled Brief. Carries `schema_version: 1` and the composition counts: cited and consulted sources, main and alternative rows, alternative findings, constraint statuses, contract gaps, checked claims, and flagged values. No claim text, field names, evidence IDs, or URLs.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| `run_health`              | INFO, at most once per run, written at teardown just before the log closes. Carries every field of `run-health.json` under `event: "run_health"`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |

Two ordinary component lines also mark the run's acquisition services. `selected search provider` is an INFO line with `provider` and `via`, written once per run because the run resolves its provider once. `page pool launched` is an INFO line carrying only the browser session ID, written once for each browser process the run's background page pool starts.

The log names the executable by basename plus a SHA-256 of its normalized canonical path and the resolver's stat fingerprint, so the same binary stays recognizable across runs without a home-directory path ever being written. It never contains a task or page URL, page text, a profile path, the full executable path, launch arguments, environment values, credentials or secrets, an error message or stack, a whole serialized error, raw helper stderr, or raw managed-install detail. The original error still propagates unchanged to the surface that may legitimately render its message.

A `tool_failure` line never carries the failure's message, a URL or URL path, tool parameters, or page text. Its `cause` is always a closed token matching `^[A-Za-z0-9_.:-]{1,80}$`: a per-tool cause such as `anomaly-challenge`, `rate-limited`, or `key-missing` for a search provider failure, or a middleware cause such as `schema-validation`, `budget:<limit>`, `evidence-frozen`, `action-phase-closed`, `per-tool-timeout`, or `unexpected:<ErrorClass>`. When a failure carries no typed cause, or its cause is not a token, the cause is derived from the stable code (`FETCH_TIMEOUT` becomes `fetch-timeout`), so every line has one. The runtime-log safety rule that bans a `cause` key admits it only in this shape, and never containing `//`, so a serialized `Error.cause` or prose under `cause` is still rejected.

That every failure reaches this line with a real cause is enforced in source, not by convention. A boundary test (`packages/agent/tests/boundaries/no-swallowed-errors.spec.ts`) scans the tool adapters under `packages/agent/src/adapters/pi/tools/` and the middleware, and fails on any bare `catch {` block or `.catch(() => undefined)` / `.catch(() => {})` unless the block maps the error to a stable `errorCode`, logs it, or rethrows it, or the site carries an inline `// swallow-ok: <reason>` comment with a non-empty reason.

#### `run-health.json`

Every agentic run that reaches teardown writes `run-health.json` beside its other artifacts. It holds counts and closed codes only — no message, URL, or page text — and its JSON Schema is emitted as `run-health.json` with the other protocol schemas.

| Field             | What it counts                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| ----------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `schema_version`  | `1`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| `run_id`          | The owning run.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| `searches`        | `total`, `ok`, `failed_by_code`, and `providers` (distinct search providers in first-use order). Only searches that were actually attempted count: a schema, evidence-phase, or action-phase refusal, and an aborted or denied call, count as neither. A search the breaker refused counts as a failed `SEARCH_BLOCKED` search. Optional: `breaker_skipped` (searches refused because the breaker was open, with no provider call) and `peak_concurrency` (most searches in flight at the provider at once).                                      |
| `fetches`         | `total` real network page fetches, `by_mode.http` and `by_mode.browser`, `repeat_fetches` (network fetches of a page already fetched earlier in the run, compared by the same canonical page identity the run's document store uses), and `failed_by_code` for failed `web_fetch` calls. Optional: `cache_hits` (reads answered from the document store with no fetch), `memo_hits` (reads answered from an earlier terminal failure with no fetch), and `challenges.http` and `challenges.browser` (challenge pages recognized at each tier).    |
| `source_failures` | Per-site read failures by stage: `fetch`, `extract`, `blocked` (robots, blocklist, rate limit, or a challenge page), `budget` (reads skipped by the run's own navigation or host budget), and `policy` (reads refused by the run's URL policy).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| `browser`         | `launches`: successful browser process launches, the task browser's and the background page pool's together. Optional: `pool_launches` (browser processes the page pool started) and `contexts` (isolated browser contexts it opened, one per background page).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| `budgets`         | `navigations_used`, `navigations_limit`, `hosts_used`, `hosts_limit`, and `exhausted` (budget limits that refused at least one call, in first-hit order). An unbounded ceiling reads as `0`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| `tool_failures`   | `total` tool calls that ended in error or timeout, and `by_code`. This is the same population the `tool_failure` lines describe.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| `notices`         | Runtime-derived notices attached to the published document; `0` when nothing was published.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| `extraction`      | Optional; present when the run returned at least one shape-aware page read or followed a discovered link. `pages_by_shape` counts page views returned by `web_fetch`, `web_search`, and `browser_extract` by shape (`article`, `collection`, `table`, `detail`, `index`); `records_shown` and `links_offered` sum what those views showed; `links_withheld` counts URLs not offered because sanitizing would have altered them; and `discovered_follows` counts successful `web_fetch` and `browser_navigate` calls to a URL a read page offered. |

Two invariants are part of the protocol `RunHealth` validation, so a file that breaks either does not validate: `searches.total` equals `searches.ok` plus the sum of `searches.failed_by_code`, and `fetches.total` equals `fetches.by_mode.http` plus `fetches.by_mode.browser`. The file is optional for every reader: run directories written before it existed have none and still render and audit unchanged. The fields marked optional above were added later, still under `schema_version: 1`; a file written before them omits them and still validates.

The same record produces the runtime notices counted in `notices`. Challenge pages add one `blocked` notice per host whose standard-browser render or `browser_extract` snapshot was a challenge, and one `other` notice per host that challenged only Yantra's HTTP client before its page was read in the browser, which discloses that second look. Every browser extraction kind checks for a challenge before returning content, links, or evidence. A browser challenge is remembered as terminal for that URL across `browser_extract`, `browser_navigate`, `web_fetch`, and inline `web_search` reads. Later attempts use that remembered failure; direct read and navigation failures carry `details.already_attempted: true` and the `already-attempted` diagnostic cause, with no new read, navigation, challenge event, or blocked notice. Searches the breaker refused are folded into the `SEARCH_BLOCKED` notice as later searches that were not attempted, rather than counted as further challenges. See [runtime notices](agentic-tasks.md#inputs-and-outputs) for the wording.

#### Usage ledger

An agentic `usage.json` records one `calls[]` entry per provider turn. Each entry has `step_id` `turn-<n>` (numbered from 1), the run's model and provider, the turn's input and output tokens, `cost_estimate_usd`, and `latency_ms`. `latency_ms` is the turn's wall time measured from the end of the previous turn, so it includes the time tools ran inside that turn and is not pure model latency. A turn whose provider reports no token counts records `0` for them, and one that reports no cost records `cost_estimate_usd: null`, which makes `totals.cost_estimate_usd` `null` for the run. The `agent` block remains the reconciled session totals: per-turn values summed when every turn reported them, otherwise the session's final usage, otherwise `null`. `provider` accepts any non-empty provider registry name, such as `groq` or `google`, not a fixed list. Older ledgers with `calls: []` still validate.

#### Tool-call records

`tool-calls.jsonl` is sanitized leaf by leaf rather than as one serialized string, so every record re-parses as JSON, and so does every `content[].text` that itself holds JSON. Each string leaf, each object key, and each JSON-in-string leaf receives the identical redaction the text sanitizer applies, so redaction is never weaker. A number that matches a sensitive pattern is redacted to its marker string. When a payload exceeds the profile's byte cap, the longest string leaves are shortened and end with `…[truncated]`; if that is not enough, tail items of the longest array are dropped and replaced by one `…[N more items truncated]` entry; a structure that still does not fit is replaced by the `…[truncated]` marker string. Serialized text is never cut mid-token.

`web_fetch` and `browser_navigate` records carry `details.provenance`, which states how the URL was attested: `match` (`exact`, `origin-root`, `query-variant`, `allowed-host`, or `none` for a refused URL) and `kind` (`goal`, `allow-host`, `tool` with the producing `tool`, `discovered`, or `none`). A `discovered` URL also names `via`, the evidence ID of the page that offered it, and `link_kind` (`pagination`, `facet`, `record`, `content`, `navigation`, `structured`, or `text`). Because the offering page's own fetch record carries its provenance too, a chain of followed links can be traced hop by hop back to the goal or a search result. The detail holds evidence IDs and closed kinds only, never page text, and the model never sees it. `web_fetch` and `browser_extract` page reads also record their `shape` and `source_id` in `details`, and an `analysis_capture_ref` when the result was trimmed to fit and the full analysis was written to `captures/`. After a partial browser extraction, `web_fetch` can return the full stored page with `details.from_store: true`, preserving its source and record IDs, adding content evidence if the earlier read returned only links, and spending no network fetch or navigation. Stored rendered content supports citation checks beyond the shorter ledger excerpt. See [Discovered-link provenance](safety-and-privacy.md#discovered-link-provenance).

A run that reaches the runtime is created before provider session startup and is finalized on typed startup failure with a failed manifest, `task_failed` event, and `report.md`. Pre-run CLI validation failures, and credential rejection performed by commands such as `do` before the runtime starts, do not guarantee a run directory.

### Errors and exit codes

| Exit  | Meaning in this feature                                                                                                                                   |
| ----- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `0`   | Diagnostic or inspection succeeded; doctor warnings and an unavailable usage index are non-fatal.                                                         |
| `1`   | Invalid command input, unknown/missing run or workflow, unreadable required audit/report artifact, or incompatible options such as smoke with `--no-llm`. |
| `2`   | A started workflow or agentic run failed, exhausted a runtime budget, or hit a non-handoff policy failure. Its run report is the primary diagnostic.      |
| `3`   | Environment failure, failed doctor check, unavailable live-smoke provider setup, or missing credentials for a command that requires an agent.             |
| `4`   | The run stopped for human handoff or user abort, such as CAPTCHA, MFA, or required consent.                                                               |
| `130` | An agentic run or live smoke was interrupted with Ctrl+C after clean teardown.                                                                            |

Stable agent startup error codes include `AGENT_MODEL_NOT_FOUND`, `AGENT_AUTH_UNAVAILABLE`, `AGENT_PROVIDER_UNAVAILABLE`, `AGENT_SESSION_START_FAILED`, and `AGENT_ABORTED`. Messages describe the failed source or configuration without printing key material.

## Configuration and Permissions

Offline agent settings resolve with the same precedence used by agentic commands: explicit flag, then `YANTRA_AGENT_*` environment variable, then profile preference, then pinned default. See [Model and authentication basics](../usage.md#model-and-authentication-basics) for the shared environment variables and credential sources.

Run directories are created with owner-only permissions (`0700`) and atomic metadata files with restrictive file permissions (`0600`) where the platform supports POSIX modes. Windows enforcement is best-effort. The history `index.db` is a rebuildable cache; run-directory files remain the source of truth.

Treat the entire run directory as sensitive. Sanitization and secret-reference logging reduce exposure, but reports, captures, workflow outputs, visited URLs, raw provider sessions, and ordinary website content can still contain personal or confidential data. Do not attach or publish a run directory without reviewing it. Yantra audit deliberately uses stable sanitized projections and does not interpret the raw provider log. `runtime.jsonl` and `run-health.json` are safe by construction — they hold no URLs, page text, paths, launch arguments, environment values, or error text, and a `tool_failure`, `fetch_challenge`, or `fetch_escalated` line names at most a bare hostname — but it is still local operator diagnostics governed by the same storage and retention policy as the rest of the run directory.

## Limitations

- Doctor has no `--fix` mode. Remediation text is advisory, and permission or credential changes remain user-controlled.
- Offline doctor credential checks establish presence, not that a provider request will succeed. Use the live, potentially billable `--agent-smoke` check for an end-to-end round trip.
- The live smoke directory lacks a normal manifest and therefore cannot be opened with `yantra show`, `yantra audit`, or `yantra report` by run ID.
- Audit requires a readable `manifest.json`. It tolerates absent optional files and skips corrupt JSONL lines, so a partial audit can omit damaged evidence instead of surfacing each malformed line as an error.
- Audit displays secret-reference keys. Those keys are not secret values, but their names may still reveal what kind of account or credential a run used.
- `show` displays only the requested tail of `events.jsonl`; it is not a replacement for audit or direct artifact inspection.
- `list` falls back to filesystem manifests when the history index is unavailable, but `usage` does not. Run directories without a valid manifest, including live-smoke directories, are omitted.
- Recorded cost is only as complete as provider reporting. Unknown local-model token and cost metrics remain `null` in the ledger's `agent` totals, and unreported per-turn cost is `null`; per-turn token counts, however, record `0` when the provider reports none, so `totals` token sums are not evidence that tokens were measured. Usage rollups treat unmetered history rows as zero cost.
- A per-turn `latency_ms` includes the tools that ran inside that turn, so it overstates model latency on tool-heavy turns.
- `report --open` starts the configured editor or platform opener asynchronously; a later editor-launch failure is reported on stderr.

For live agent-runtime behavior, failures, and handoffs, see [Agentic Tasks with `yantra do`](agentic-tasks.md).
